info.title: Actio
info.description:
Actio's HTTP API, which its web app is built on.

- **Sessions.** Everything but the health checks needs a session, a guest's included.
  It lives in a cookie: start one with `POST /api/session/guest`. Without one the
  answer is 401.
- **Errors.** Every error is an RFC 9457 problem document (`application/problem+json`):
  see the `Problem` schema. A request that changes something, sent by a page on another
  site, is answered 403.
- **Answers from a model** are streamed: see `POST /api/conversations/{id}/turns`. An
  answer is written whether or not anyone reads along. It can be joined again, and
  stopped, by the turn's id.
- **Usage is limited** per session and per week. `GET /api/usage` says how much is
  left, and a question that no longer fits is answered 429, with when it will. A plan
  may also limit how many answers are written for one account at once, and an account
  reads along with only so many at once: past either, the answer is 429 too.

get.description: Answers whenever the process can serve requests.

200 when the database is reachable and migrated, Valkey answers, and the worker
works, where this process runs one inside it; 503 otherwise.

post.description:
Start a session as a new guest, and set its cookie.

A browser that already has a live session keeps it and gets 200: opening the page
twice doesn't create two guests. 429 when too many guests were created from the
client's address.

429.description: Too many attempts. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: Attempts can't be counted right now, so this one is refused.

post.description:
Create a lasting account, and log in to it.

A guest who signs up keeps the same account id and everything it owns. 409 when the
address is already registered, or when this session already has an account. 429
when too many sign-ups were tried from the client's address.

409.description: The email address has an account, or you are logged in to one.

429.description: Too many attempts. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: Attempts can't be counted right now, so this one is refused.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

post.description:
Log in with an email address and a password, and set a new session's cookie.

401 for an unknown address and for a wrong password alike. The session this browser
had before, if any, ends. A guest's is deleted with the guest, whose conversations
move to the account.

429 after too many attempts from the client's address, or for this email address
from anywhere. Every attempt counts, right or wrong, and a refused one isn't checked
at all: the right password gets a 429 too.

429.description: Too many attempts. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: Attempts can't be counted right now, so this one is refused.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

delete.description:
Log out of this browser, and clear its cookie. A guest's account is deleted.

Always 204: ending a session that is already gone is not an error.

put.description:
Change the password. Every other browser is logged out; this one gets a new cookie.

403 when the current password is wrong; 409 for a guest, who has none. 429 after
too many password attempts for this account, logins included.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

409.description: A guest has no password to change.

429.description: Too many attempts. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: Attempts can't be counted right now, so this one is refused.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

get.description: Who you are, according to your session cookie. 401 without a live session.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

delete.description: Log out of every browser at once, this one included.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

get.description:
Your conversations, most recently active first, a page at a time. While a
conversation's title is on its way, its `title_pending` says so.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

get.description: One conversation, with the messages of the branch that is shown.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

404.description: No such conversation, or it isn't yours.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

patch.description: Give the conversation a title. Its place in the list doesn't change.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

404.description: No such conversation, or it isn't yours.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

delete.description:
Delete the conversation and every message in it, on every branch. There is no
way back.

An answer that is being written in it is stopped first: nobody could read it. What
it had used until then is counted, as for any answer that is stopped.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

404.description: No such conversation, or it isn't yours.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

put.description:
Show the branch that passes through a message: another version of a question,
or of an answer, and what followed it. Where that branch forks again further down,
the newest version is shown.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

404.description: No such conversation, or no such message in it.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

post.description:
Ask a model something, and stream its answer.

When the model can't answer before its first word, a model asked in its place does,
as `GET /api/models` lists them (`then`). The turn is the asked model's all the
same, and costs what a question to it costs: its `answered_by` says which model
wrote the answer.

The answer is written whether or not this response is read to its end. To stop it,
cancel the turn: closing the connection doesn't.

200.description: The answer, as the AI SDK's UI message stream, version 1.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

404.description: No such conversation, or no such message in it.

409.description: The message was sent before, or an answer is still being written.

429.description: Too many messages in a short time, or a usage limit is reached. `Retry-After` says how long to wait. For a usage limit, `window` names the one that is full, `resets_at` says when it starts over, and `alternatives` lists the models that cost nothing. Or as many answers are being written as the plan allows at once, which `at_once` says: nobody knows when one ends, so there is no `Retry-After`. Or no model that could answer can take the message right now, the installation having reached the limits of its models' providers: `model` names the model asked, and `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: The model can't answer right now, nor can any model asked in its place: `model_status` says why the model itself can't. Or messages, or usage, can't be counted right now, or an answer couldn't be read along with.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

get.description:
Read along with a turn that is being written: after a reload, after a lost
connection, or from another window.

The stream starts at the answer's first event, whenever it is joined, so that it
can be read by itself.

200.description: The answer that is being written, from its beginning, in the same format as the turn's own response.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

204.description: Nothing is being written: the turn has ended. Read the conversation for what it left.

404.description: No such conversation, or no such turn in it.

429.description: The account already has six readers open, or more: responses that read along with a turn. Those of the requests that started the turns count, and are never refused.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

post.description:
Stop a turn that is being written. What it had written is kept, and counted.

Answers once the turn is recorded, with the turn as it is then: `stopped`. A turn
that had ended already is left as it ended, and answered the same way. So is one
that this server can't stop, because the process that was writing it is gone: it
says `running` until it is given up on, a minute after it was last heard from.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

404.description: No such conversation, or no such turn in it.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

get.description:
The models you can choose from, whether each can answer right now, by itself or
through a model asked in its place, what the shortest question to each would meet
right now, and what each costs.

Each provider is asked at most every 15 seconds, so this can be fetched often.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

post.description:
Have a model loaded into its server's memory now, so that the first question to
it doesn't wait for the load. A local server keeps a model loaded for a few minutes
after it was last asked anything; this moves that time too.

Answers at once, without waiting for the load, and with no body. It costs no
credits. What becomes of the load isn't said: a question asked meanwhile waits for
it at the server, as it would have waited for its own.

202.description: The model is being loaded: a load was started, or one is under way already.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

204.description: Nothing was started: the model's kind of server can't be asked to load a model ahead, or its server is writing as many answers as it takes, or the model can't answer and a model asked in its place would, which is never loaded ahead.

429.description: Too many requests to load a model in a short time. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: The model can't answer right now, nor can any model asked in its place: `model_status` says why the model itself can't. Or requests can't be counted right now.

422.description: The request doesn't have the expected form. `errors` lists what is wrong, and where.

get.description: Your plan, and how much of each of its limits you have used.

401.description: No session, or it has ended. Start one with `POST /api/session/guest`.

503.description: Usage can't be read right now.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. Empty on the last page.

title.title: Title
title.description: Empty until the conversation is named.

title_pending.title: Title Pending
title_pending.description:
Whether a model was asked for the conversation's title a moment ago, and none has
come yet: the list is worth reading again shortly. False again after 15 seconds at
most, whatever became of the title.

last_active_at.title: Last Active At
last_active_at.description: When a message was last added. The list is ordered by it.

current_leaf_id.title: Current Leaf Id
current_leaf_id.description: The last message of the branch that is shown.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: That branch, from its first message to its last.

unanswered.description:
When the branch ends with a question: the last turn that tried to answer it. It
says whether an answer is still being written, or why none came. Otherwise empty.

title.title: Title
title.description: Empty until the conversation is named.

title_pending.title: Title Pending
title_pending.description:
Whether a model was asked for the conversation's title a moment ago, and none has
come yet: the list is worth reading again shortly. False again after 15 seconds at
most, whatever became of the title.

last_active_at.title: Last Active At
last_active_at.description: When a message was last added. The list is ordered by it.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: The message this one follows. Empty for a first message.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description:
Every version of this message, oldest first, itself included: the messages
that follow the same one. Show another with `PUT …/branch`.

turn.description: For an answer: the turn that wrote it.

MessageOut.title: MessageOut
MessageOut.description:
A message, in the shape the web app's chat library reads: `id`, `role`, `parts`,
and everything of Actio's own under `metadata`.

default.title: Default
default.description: The `id` of the model that is used when a request names none.

id.title: Id
id.description: The name to ask for it by, such as `standard`.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: What kind of server runs it.

model.title: Model
model.description: Its name on that server: for Ollama, what `ollama pull` takes.

context_window.title: Context Window
context_window.description:
How many tokens of a conversation the model takes here: its context window, which
holds the conversation and its answer, or what its server takes from this
installation's account in a minute, when that is less. A request larger than that, by
an estimate of its tokens, isn't sent to it while another model that may answer the
same question can take it.

then.title: Then
then.description:
The `id`s of the models asked in its place, in this order, when it can't answer
before the first word of an answer: its server is away, too busy, or refuses. Empty
for a model that has none.

status.title: Status

thinking.title: Thinking
thinking.description:
Whether a question to it can ask for reasoning: whether, of itself and the models
asked in its place, the first in that order that can answer right now can reason
before it answers. That one says it also when another would be given the question
first (`asked_first`). While none of them can answer, whether it can itself: false
while its server can't be asked.

asked_first.title: Asked First
asked_first.description:
The `id` of the model the shortest question to it would be given to first, right
now: itself, or one of `then`, which is given it while this model can't answer, has
nothing left of what its provider lets this installation send it, or keeps failing
while that one doesn't. `null` when nobody would be asked: none of them can answer,
which `status` says, or the question would be refused for now, which `retry_after`
says. A longer question may be given to another.

failing.title: Failing
failing.description:
Whether the model `asked_first` names keeps failing: enough of the latest
requests to it failed that, for a while, it is asked after models that don't. It is
given the question first all the same: no model that would do better is there to
ask before it. False when `asked_first` is `null`.

retry_after.title: Retry After
retry_after.description:
For how long the shortest question to it would be refused for now, in whole
seconds, as the refusal of a question asked now would say: every model that could
take it has reached what its provider lets this installation send it. `null` when
the question would be asked, and when none of them can answer. A longer question
may be refused for longer, or where this one isn't.

price.description:
What a question to it is counted at: its own price, also when a model asked in
its place answers. All three are 0 for a model that costs nothing.

id.title: Id
id.description: Chosen by the sender. Sending the same message again doesn't ask twice.

NewMessage.title: NewMessage
NewMessage.description: A question, as its sender made it.

title.title: Title
title.description: What to call it, such as `Free`.

input.title: Input
input.description: For what it reads: the conversation so far.

output.title: Output
output.description: For what it writes: its answer, and its reasoning.

cached_input.title: Cached Input
cached_input.description:
For what its server says it read again from its cache. The same as `input` where
no other price is stated for it.

PriceOut.title: PriceOut
PriceOut.description: What a model costs, in credits per million tokens.

Readiness.title: Readiness
Readiness.description:
What is missing, by name. Never why: a failure's details go to the log, because
they can name hosts and users.

`worker` is there only in a process that runs the worker inside it, as
`actio --role all` does. It is `not working` before the worker has said that it
works, from the moment the worker ends with an error or can't work until it says so
again, and once it hasn't said so for 20 seconds, whatever it is doing.

ReasoningPart.title: ReasoningPart
ReasoningPart.description:
What a model thought before answering. Shown apart from the answer, and never
sent back to a model as if it had been said.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Any message of the branch to show.

TextPart.title: TextPart
TextPart.description: Text for the reader: a person's message, or a model's answer.

model.title: Model
model.description:
The model that was asked, by its `id` in `GET /api/models`. The turn is its own
whoever answered, and costs what a question to it costs.

answered_by.title: Answered By
answered_by.description:
The model that answered, by its `id` in `GET /api/models`: the one that was
asked, or one asked in its place (`then`) because that one couldn't answer before
its first word. A model that ended its answer without writing a word has answered
too. Empty while the turn runs; when no model answered, because every one failed
before its first word, or the turn was stopped or interrupted while it waited; for a
turn that was given up on; and for turns recorded before this was kept.

thinking.title: Thinking
thinking.description: Whether the model was asked to reason before answering.

status.title: Status
status.description:
`running` while the answer is written. Then `completed`; `stopped`, because
whoever asked stopped it; `failed`, because the model did; or `interrupted`, because
the server that was writing it was restarted, or stopped answering.

finish_reason.title: Finish Reason
finish_reason.description:
Why the answer of a completed turn ended. `stop`: the model had finished.
`length`: it ran into the limit on a single answer's size. `context_window`: the
conversation and the answer together filled the model's context window. A model's
server that doesn't count what it read and wrote says `length` for both limits, and
so do turns recorded before the two were told apart. `time_limit`: the model was
still writing when its server's time for a whole answer was over, and the answer
stops there. A provider may give other reasons, such as `content_filter`.

error.title: Error
error.description:
For a failed turn, what went wrong, as a code: `model_unavailable`,
`model_missing`, `context_overflow`, `model_refused`, `answer_interrupted`,
`model_too_slow`, `model_error`, `internal_error`. `model_too_slow`: its server's
time for a whole answer was over before the model had written anything.

context_tokens.title: Context Tokens
context_tokens.description:
About how many tokens of the context window of the model that answered,
`answered_by`, the conversation takes after this turn: what the model was shown, and
the words it answered with. What it only thought isn't kept for the next question,
and isn't counted: where it thought and then answered, the words' share of what it
wrote is a guess, by characters. Empty while the turn runs, and when the model's
server counted nothing, as for a stopped or failed turn, or one whose answer was cut
at its time.

credits.title: Credits
credits.description:
What the turn cost you, in credits: see `GET /api/usage`. `0` for a model that
costs nothing. Empty while it runs, and when nothing was counted for it: a turn that
failed or was interrupted, or one that wrote nothing and whose model's server
counted nothing.

capped_by_usage.title: Capped By Usage
capped_by_usage.description:
Whether a usage limit left the answer less room than the model allows. With the
`finish_reason` `length`, that is why the answer was cut.

first_word_at.title: First Word At
first_word_at.description:
When the first piece of the answer came, its reasoning included, by the server's
clock. From `started_at`, that is how long the first word took: the wait for the
model's server included. Empty while the turn runs, when the model wrote nothing,
and for a turn that was given up on.

TurnOut.title: TurnOut
TurnOut.description: One attempt to answer a question: which model was asked, and how it ended.

message.description: A new question to add and answer.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: With `message`: the answer it follows. Left out for a first question.

answer_to.title: Answer To
answer_to.description: Instead of `message`: a question that is already there, to answer again.

model.title: Model
model.description: A model's `id` from `GET /api/models`. Left out: the default one.

thinking.title: Thinking
thinking.description: Ask the model to reason before it answers, if it can.

windows.title: Windows
windows.description:
The limits of the plan, each of which a question has to fit in. A plan without
limits has none.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: How many credits the window allows.

used.title: Used
used.description:
How many are used up. It can pass `limit` by a little: an answer is counted for
what it really used, which is known only when it has been written.

reserved.title: Reserved
reserved.description:
How many are held for answers that are being written right now. They are not
available either, until those answers end and are counted.

resets_at.title: Resets At
resets_at.description:
When the window starts over, with nothing used. Empty for a session that isn't
open: the next question that costs something opens it.

WindowOut.title: WindowOut
WindowOut.description: One limit: so many credits, until the window starts over.

Problem.description:
An error, as RFC 9457 problem details. Every error this API answers looks like
this. Some carry more members: `errors` (422: what is wrong with the request, and
where), `retry_after` (429: seconds to wait), `window`, `resets_at` and
`alternatives` (429: the usage limit that is reached, when it starts over, and the
models that cost nothing), `at_once` (429: how many answers the plan allows to be
written at once), `model` and `model_status` (503: the model that can't answer),
`model` alone (429: the model asked, when no model that could answer can take the
message right now), `turn_id` and `turn_status` (409: the turn in the way).

type.description: Always `about:blank`: the status says what kind of problem it is.
type.title: Type

title.description: The status in words, such as `Not Found`.
title.title: Title

detail.description: What happened this time, in words a person can act on.
detail.title: Detail

Problem.title: Problem
